findings.detail: Both steps that reach AMD from a mechanism have polarity 'unknown', although the mechanisms state them as positive ('driving macular degeneration', 'contributing to the geographic atrophy'), so no arm of any hypothesis can reach the disease.

All five GWAS rows (rs2414577, rs17231506, rs11569415, rs36212733, rs13278062) are cited at mechanism steps (gene to process, process to AMD); each reports only a variant-AMD association and states none of those steps.
Open Targets gene-AMD scores (CETP, LIPC, C3, TNFRSF10A) are cited for process-to-AMD steps; they score genes, not lipid metabolism, complement activation or apoptosis, and carry no direction.

The run's strongest evidence is five signed GWAS rows (rs36212733-C beta increase; rs2414577-C, rs17231506-T, rs11569415-A, rs13278062-T beta decrease), but no chain has a variant step, so this evidence supports nothing the run states.

The run leaves 'lipid metabolism', 'complement activation', 'apoptosis', 'retinal pigment epithelium' and the falsification readout 'drusen' as kind 'other' with no CURIE, though exact terms exist (GO:0006629, GO:0006956, GO:0006915, CL:0002586, HP:0011510).

The shared node 'lipid metabolism' joins LIPC (lipid hydrolysis, a lipid metabolic process) and CETP (lipid transfer between lipoproteins, which GO files under lipid transport), so the hub hides two different mechanisms and the CETP step has no stated direction.

The title and mechanism say only that variants 'alter' lipid handling, so the hypothesis makes no directional claim for LIPC or CETP; the falsification test alone implies CETP promotes drusen, and nothing gives LIPC a direction.
Curator knowledge, not from a cited text: wild-type mice have no CETP, so 'inhibit CETP in a mouse model of AMD' needs a CETP-transgenic mouse, which the run does not mention.
ARMS2 enters the chain only by binding C3, which has no direction, so the chain never says whether ARMS2 raises or lowers complement activation and the ARMS2 claim cannot compose.

The only paper the run cites (PMID:42171393) places TNFRSF10A expression in endothelial cells of AMD tissue, not in the retinal pigment epithelium the hypothesis is about, and never mentions apoptosis.

The RPE context sits only on the disease step of each chain, not on the step that produces complement activation or apoptosis; if that context is read as limiting the step (a refinement), the chains would not connect even if the disease steps had signs.
No hypothesis cites any supporting or contradicting evidence outside its chain (both lists are empty for all three), so nothing against any hypothesis was sought.

The abstention for MCF2L2 and CACNA1E cites GWAS:MCF2L2:no-association, GWAS:CACNA1E:no-association and OT:CACNA1E-MONDO_0005150, none of which is in sources.json, so the abstention's grounds cannot be read.
The format has no place for a run's abstention (genes covered, reason, cited evidence), so an abstention can be neither checked nor counted.

The guide takes a claim's sign from the title or mechanism only; it does not say whether a falsification's expected direction (inhibit CETP, drusen fall) may supply the sign, so lipid_metabolism gets no claim.

GWAS Catalog rows label an allele 'riskAlleleName' while the beta says 'decrease' for a case-control trait (rs2414577-C, rs17231506-T, rs11569415-A, rs13278062-T), and give the beta in 'unit' with no statement that it is a log odds ratio; a curator converting these to allele directions needs a rule for both.
STRING C3-ARMS2 counts as curatedDb because its experimental channel (0.24) clears the 0.15 threshold, though text-mining (0.62) supplies most of the combined 0.70 score.

An enzyme that catalyzes one reaction class within a broad process (LIPC, lipid hydrolysis) becomes 'LIPC raises lipid metabolism'; participation (RO:0000056) would say it better, but the guide maps a leads_to step to an effect.

The mechanism says the variants alter 'local lipid handling in the retina', but both texts the run cites place LIPC and CETP in blood: LIPC acts on 'circulating plasma lipoproteins' and CETP is 'Secreted in plasma' and moves lipids between plasma lipoproteins; nothing cited puts either in the retina.

The title's own claim, altered lipid metabolism promotes drusen formation, is not a step: the chain jumps from 'lipid metabolism' to an unsigned association with AMD, and drusen appears only as the falsification readout.

The run treats each GWAS row as evidence for its 'mapped gene' without checking: the rs2414577 record's Ensembl context puts the variant inside ALDH1A2 (distance 0), 22-44 kb from LIPC, and rs36212733 lies in ARMS2 while the record flags HTRA1 (3-6 kb away) as the closest gene, so position alone does not tie either signal to the gene the run names, and no cited text does.

The guide defines no_sign as 'a causal step with no direction anywhere', but its leads_to rule sends a step to no_sign whenever no cited text gives the direction; these two steps have a direction in the mechanism and none in a cited text, so the two rules disagree on them.
